title: Number of full-time equivalent students enroll in postsecondary institutions annually
notes: This table presents data collected from Title IV institutions in the United States.

This is the full-time equivalent enrollment at institutions from July 1 of one year through June 30 of the next. Prior to 2010-11, institutions could choose to report on the 12-month period between July 1 and June 30 or September 1 and August 31. The full-time-equivalent (FTE) enrollment displayed in this table is calculated from institutions’ instructional activity over a 12-month period. For institutions following a quarter calendar system, 45 undergraduate credit hours is considered one undergraduate FTE and 36 graduate credit hours is considered one graduate FTE. For institutions following a semester, trimester, 4-1-4, or other academic year calendar system, 30 undergraduate credit hours is considered one undergraduate FTE and 24 graduate credit hours is considered one graduate FTE. For all calendar systems (both academic year-based systems and continuous enrollment systems), 900 undergraduate contact hours is considered one undergraduate FTE. Definitions for terms used in this table may be found in the IPEDS online glossary located at https://surveys.nces.ed.gov/ipeds/VisGlossaryAll.aspx.

SOURCE: U.S. Department of Education, National Center for Education Statistics, Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), 12-month Enrollment component final data (2009-10 - 2023-24) and provisional data (2024-25).

title: Adjusted 9-month average salary
notes: This table presents data collected from Title IV degree-granting institutions in the United States.

Full-time instructional staff includes those on 9-, 10-, 11-, or 12-month contracts.  Total salary outlays for full-time instructional staff  on 10-, 11-, and 12-month contracts were adjusted to 9-month outlays by dividing the outlay for the longer contracts by their length and multiplying the result by 9. The “equated” outlays were then added to the outlays for 9-month staff, and the resulting sum was then divided by the total number of staff to determine an average salary. Salaries for staff on less-than-9-month contracts were not collected.
Full-time instructional staff from administrative offices are included.
Amounts displayed are in current dollars.

SOURCE: U.S. Department of Education, National Center for Education Statistics, Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), Human Resources component final data (fall 2016 - 2023) and provisional data (fall 2024).

title: The total core expenses per full-time equivalent enrollment of public and private not-for-profit postsecondary institutions
notes: This table presents data from Title IV institutions in the United States

Beginning in fiscal year 2010, expenses by functional categories under GASB and FASB reporting standards were aligned to allow comparisons of data across institutions. Public institutions reporting either GASB or FASB reporting standards or private not-for-profit institutions using FASB reporting standards are included. Core expenses are the expenses for the essential education activities of the institution. Core expenses include expenses for instruction, research, public service, academic support, student services, institutional support, scholarships and fellowships (GASB) or net grant aid to students (FASB)  and other expenses. Core expenses exclude expenses for auxiliary enterprises, hospitals, and independent operations.
Expenses from administrative offices are excluded.
Amounts displayed are in current dollars.

SOURCE: U.S. Department of Education, National Center for Education Statistics, Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), Data Feedback Report, Derived variables from Finance component final data (fiscal years 2010 - 2023) and provisional data (fiscal year 2024) and 12-month Enrollment component final data (2009-10 – 2022-23) and provisional data (2023-24).
